question: Cisco full-time (Software Engineer Grade 4), final ETR round of about 15 minutes with HR, over almost as soon as it began. Reported: the HR explained the **breakdown of the CTC**, and asked about the **notice period**, **previous work experience**, **interest in higher studies**, and **location preference**.
lookingFor: Clear, consistent facts about your own situation (notice period, dates, experience).
Genuine commitment to joining and staying with the company.
Reasonable flexibility and professionalism around compensation and location.
No surprises: honesty that matches earlier rounds and your resume.
answer:
This round is mostly confirmation. Prepare facts and a calm, honest tone.

**CTC breakdown.** CTC (cost to company) is the total yearly cost of an employee and usually includes fixed pay (basic, allowances such as HRA), variable pay or bonus, benefits (insurance, retirement contributions such as PF) and possibly joining or stock components. Ask HR to explain parts you do not understand: which parts are fixed, which are variable and on what basis, and what the in-hand pay will approximately be. Do not negotiate aggressively in an ETR round; if you have questions, ask politely, and keep a written copy of the figures. Check the offer letter later against what you were told.

**Notice period.** State it exactly as in your contract, and say whether it is negotiable or buy-out is possible. If you are a fresher, say you are available from the joining date given by the company. Never guess; check your contract before the round.

**Previous experience.** Give a 30-second summary that matches your resume: company, role, main technologies and one notable result. Keep it consistent with what you said in the technical and managerial rounds.

**Higher studies.** The company is checking retention. Answer honestly and with commitment: if you have no plans, say so and explain that you want to grow through work; if you are considering it, say it is a future possibility, not a plan that conflicts with joining. Do not promise what you do not mean.

**Location preference.** Give a first preference with a practical reason, and show openness to the other locations. Hiring depends on team needs, so rigid answers can cost you.

**Mistakes to avoid:** inconsistent dates, exaggerating your salary or experience (details are verified in background checks), sounding unsure about whether you will join, and trying to bargain without data. Have 1-2 questions on onboarding or the team ready.
followUps: What salary or offer have you received elsewhere, if any?
Can you join earlier than your notice period ends?
Why are you leaving your current job?
Do you have any concerns about the offer or the location?
